items.title: Independent technique validates landmark M87* image
items.excerpt: A CSIRO team used machine-learning and AI techniques to reanalyse the 2019 Event Horizon Telescope data and recovered a black-hole ring nearly identical to the original image, supporting that the ring is real rather than a processing artifact (Nature).
items.rationale: Nature-published ML reanalysis independently confirms the first black-hole image — high-credibility, broadly resonant astronomy result.

items.title: Preserving human involvement at the start of a creative task can improve AI-assisted outcomes
items.excerpt: In a PNAS Nexus experiment with 285 students, Wharton's Hosanagar and Ahn found ChatGPT cut story-writing time 36%, but stories were better only when humans kept ideation and outlining or had flexible AI help; merely approving AI drafts produced worse stories.
items.rationale: Most actionable item in the pool: controlled PNAS Nexus evidence that keeping ideation/outlining human yields better AI-assisted creative work.

items.title: AI-written peer reviews outscored top human experts in blind comparisons, Harvard working paper finds
items.excerpt: In blind comparisons, both an AI judge and former journal editors preferred AI-written reviews of unpublished research papers over reviews by well-paid human experts in the large majority of cases.
items.rationale: New blind-comparison study on AI peer review quality — fresh, provocative research-method story distinct from the 11-05 paper-generator item.

items.title: New research could lead to faster, trustworthy AI models for climate prediction
items.excerpt: An MIT training technique trains climate emulators on deliberately unrealistic emissions scenarios, boosting accuracy and adaptability to unfamiliar futures while using only a fraction of the usual training data.
items.rationale: Counter-intuitive MIT training method (unrealistic scenarios → better emulators with less data); a different study from the 11-06 atmosphere-emulator card.

items.title: Q-CTRL Demonstrates Push-Button Cold-Start Calibration on QuantWare Superconducting QPUs
items.excerpt: Q-CTRL's physics-informed AI state machine in Boulder Opal autonomously calibrated a 21-qubit QuantWare Contralto-D21 from an uncalibrated state to operational gate fidelities, detecting anomalies and recovering underperforming qubits.
items.rationale: Concrete autonomous-calibration demo on real hardware; quantum slot, distinct from published decoder/circuit-reduction stories.
